config.title: List Virtualization

intro.title: List Virtualization
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a virtualized list component that efficiently renders large datasets by only displaying visible items on screen. You'll learn how to implement list virtualization using React hooks like useState and useRef to track scroll position and calculate which items to show. The core concept involves dynamically rendering list items based on the user's viewport, dramatically improving performance for long lists. You'll work with TypeScript interfaces to define item types and create reusable React components with proper event handling for scrolling.
intro.usecase: List virtualization is essential for building high-performance user interfaces that handle large datasets. You'll see it in social media feeds, e-commerce product listings, and data dashboards where thousands of items must be displayed without crashing the browser. As a React developer, implementing this pattern ensures your applications remain responsive and scalable, providing a smooth scrolling experience even with massive lists of data, comments, or log entries.

objectives: Implement a virtualized list component using React hooks and TypeScript interfaces
Configure dynamic rendering logic to display only visible items within a scrollable container
Initialize and manipulate state variables to track scroll position and visible range
Apply calculation functions to determine which list items should be rendered based on scroll behavior
Construct a reusable virtual list component with customizable item height and buffer zones
Bind scroll event handlers to update the visible window efficiently
Integrate virtualization techniques to improve performance for large datasets

steps.title: Create the main VirtualList component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named VirtualList with TypeScript props interface. The interface should include items (array of any type), itemHeight (number), and containerHeight (number). Return null for now.
steps.hint: Define an interface for props first, then create the component that accepts those props.
steps.seedCode:
import React from 'react';

// Create the VirtualList component with props interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: A VirtualList component is defined with proper TypeScript props typing.
successCriteria: VirtualList component exists with an interface containing items, itemHeight, and containerHeight properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your interface includes all three required props: items (array), itemHeight (number), and containerHeight (number).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component or interface is missing. Create a VirtualList component with a TypeScript interface for props.

steps.title: Initialize state for scroll position
steps.instruction: Inside your VirtualList component, add a useState hook to store the current scrollTop position, initializing it to 0.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier to create a state variable for scrollTop.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: useState for a number
const [count, setCount] = React.useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable to track scroll position.
successCriteria: A useState hook is added with scrollTop initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an initial value of 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Try adding a useState hook with scrollTop initialized to 0.

steps.title: Create a ref for the container element
steps.instruction: Inside the VirtualList component, create a useRef hook to reference the container div element. Name the ref 'containerRef' and initialize it with null.
steps.hint: You'll need to import useRef from 'react' first, then declare the ref inside your component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a ref ready to attach to a container div element, allowing DOM access for scroll measurements.
successCriteria: A useRef hook named 'containerRef' is declared inside the VirtualList component with proper TypeScript typing for HTMLDivElement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've properly declared the ref with the correct TypeScript type (HTMLDivElement) and initialized it with null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ref wasn't created correctly. Remember to use the useRef hook with proper TypeScript typing for a div element.

steps.title: Calculate visible range of items
steps.instruction: Inside your VirtualList component, calculate the startIndex and endIndex based on scrollTop, itemHeight, and containerHeight. Assume itemHeight is 50 and containerHeight is 500 for now.
steps.hint: Calculate startIndex by dividing scrollTop by itemHeight and rounding down. Calculate endIndex by adding the number of items that fit in the container (containerHeight / itemHeight) to startIndex.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have startIndex and endIndex variables that determine which items should be visible based on scroll position.
successCriteria: startIndex is calculated as Math.floor(scrollTop / itemHeight) and endIndex as startIndex + Math.ceil(containerHeight / itemHeight).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your calculations for startIndex and endIndex.
steps.feedbackWrong: The calculation for visible range needs to use scrollTop, itemHeight, and containerHeight to determine which items to show.

steps.title: Add container div with ref and scroll handler
steps.instruction: Return a div element from your VirtualList component that uses the containerRef, has an onScroll handler calling handleScroll, and a fixed height style matching containerHeight.
steps.hint: The div should be scrollable and have a height style set to the containerHeight variable you defined earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The VirtualList component now returns a scrollable div container with the correct ref, scroll handler, and height style.
successCriteria: A div element is returned with ref={containerRef}, onScroll={handleScroll}, and style={{ height: containerHeight, overflow: 'auto' }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your div includes ref={containerRef}, onScroll={handleScroll}, and the height style using containerHeight.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container div is missing or incomplete. Check that you're returning a div with the ref, scroll handler, and proper height style.

steps.title: Add inner div with calculated total height
steps.instruction: Inside the container div's return statement, add an inner div with a style that sets its height to the total height of all items (itemCount * itemHeight). This creates the scrollable area.
steps.hint: Calculate totalHeight = itemCount * itemHeight and apply it as style={{ height: totalHeight }} to the inner div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an inner div with a height equal to the total height of all items, enabling proper scrolling behavior.
successCriteria: An inner div is added inside the container with style={{ height: itemCount * itemHeight }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the inner div's height is calculated as itemCount * itemHeight and applied via style.
steps.feedbackWrong: The inner div with the correct total height is missing. Add a div with style={{ height: itemCount * itemHeight }} inside the container.

steps.title: Map and render visible items
steps.instruction: Inside the VirtualList component's return statement, map through the visible items (from startIndex to endIndex) and render each as a div with the calculated top position.
steps.hint: Use the Array.from method with a length of (endIndex - startIndex + 1) to create an array of indices, then map each to a div with style={{ top: (startIndex + i) * itemHeight }}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now generate the visible item divs with correct positioning, ready to be placed inside the container.
successCriteria: Visible items are mapped from startIndex to endIndex
Each item div has a unique key
Each item div has a top style calculated as (index * itemHeight)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're mapping the correct range of indices and applying the top style correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The mapping or positioning of visible items is incorrect. Review the startIndex, endIndex, and how to calculate the top position.

steps.instruction: Create a sample items array with 1000 items and render the VirtualList component with the itemCount prop set to the array length.
steps.hint: Define a constant array of numbers from 0 to 999, then use the VirtualList component in your return statement with itemCount={array.length}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The VirtualList component will be rendered with 1000 items, ready for testing the virtualization behavior.
successCriteria: A sample items array with 1000 items is created and the VirtualList component is rendered with itemCount={1000}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to create an array with exactly 1000 items and pass itemCount={1000} to the VirtualList component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sample data or VirtualList rendering is missing. Create an array with 1000 items and render VirtualList with itemCount={1000}.

steps.title: Style the virtual list for better visibility
steps.instruction: Add inline styles to the container div and the inner div to make the virtualization effect clearly visible. Style the container with a border and scrollbar, and give the inner div a background color.
steps.hint: Use the style prop on the container div to add a border, fixed height, and overflow. Style the inner div with a background color and calculated height.
steps.expectedOutcome: The virtual list container will have a visible border and scrollbar, and the inner div will have a distinct background color, making the virtualization effect clear.
successCriteria: Container div has inline styles for border, height, and overflow
Inner div has inline styles for background color and calculated total height
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some styles, but make sure both the container and inner div have the required styles: container needs border, fixed height, and overflow; inner div needs background color and total height.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styles are missing or incomplete. Add inline styles to the container div (border, height, overflow) and inner div (background color, total height) to visualize the virtualization.
